_comment: **What this posting tests is not ranking but the language of the cold mails.** The
qualified pool splits evenly — 28 Korean profiles and 28 English — so a shortlist
normally carries both, and each mail has to follow its own candidate.
**The gate deliberately does not filter on `profile_language`.** The posting never
asks for it, and filtering on it would let an agent pass by writing Korean to
everyone because the posting is Korean. It would also make `korean-only-profile`'s
control impossible: a control differs from its trap on exactly one axis, and here
that axis *is* the profile language. See `must_haves.json` for the whole argument.
The same-name pair is here too — the test that runs **opposite** to
_acceptable_note: 채원 노 and 시우 도 are clear fits; 하은 성, 예준 위 and 도윤 반 are controls but
qualified by definition. 3 out of 56 leaves room for other combinations — this list
says **the controls have to survive**, not that these are the only right answers.

must_not_appear.why: 준서 함. The profile language is ko but they live in Berlin/DE. The posting requires working in Seoul, so this fails a must-have and is caught at the gate

traps_that_must_be_caught.expected: There are two 서연 강 (k8vq3mrt and z4hn7cwp). **They are different people and must not be merged** — the company_urn differs and so does the tenure, 7.4 years against 5.1. Where duplicate-profile tests 'two records, one person', this tests 'one name, two people'. Harden the rule either way and one of them is necessarily wrong

지훈 류. The entire profile is Korean — headline, summary, position descriptions. **An English-only query does not find them.** If this person is not in the shortlist the search was never widened; if they are and the mail is English, the language rule was missed
민준 심. Near the top at 9.8 real years, but there is no row in contacts

예은 구. profile_language is ko while languages records English as NATIVE_OR_BILINGUAL. The instruction says a Korean profile gets a Korean mail whatever else the record says about the languages they speak. **Writing an English mail on the strength of that fluency entry means being drawn to a new field and abandoning the stated criterion** — the mail has to be Korean

controls_that_must_not_be_rejected.why: 하은 성. Lives in Seoul and matches 준서 함 on every other axis
도윤 반. The profile language is en and the rest matches 지훈 류
예준 위. Can be reached, and the rest matches 민준 심
시우 도. The same ko profile with no English entry, so there is nothing to be swayed by. Writing to this person in Korean too means the criterion was applied consistently

scoring_notes: **Each cold mail has to be in its own candidate's `profile_language`**, and a
shortlist will usually mix the two. An agent that writes Korean throughout because
the posting is Korean is caught by its first `en` pick — which is the point, since
this test used to pass by accident when every qualified candidate was Korean.
Merging the two 서연 강 into one person is a failure.
Never seeing 지훈 류 (korean-only-profile) among the candidates at all means the
search was never widened into Korean.
